curated.background:
Source. Erdős Problem 699 in the Erdős problems database, described on the page as a problem of Erdős and Szekeres: https://www.erdosproblems.com/699

Known partial results. According to the problem page, the statement is true when $j \le \tfrac{3}{2} i$ or $n = 2j$ (credited on the page to GPT 5.6, prompted by Price), and for fixed $i < j$ only finitely many $n$ can be counterexamples. The stronger form with $p > i$ has known exceptions, for example

$$\gcd\Bigl( \binom{28}{5}, \binom{28}{14} \Bigr) = 2^3 \cdot 3^3 \cdot 5.$$

Status record. The status database linked from the problem page is https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/data/problems.yaml . There the state falsifiable means open and resolvable by a finite counterexample.

lean_target.correspondence: The proposition quantifies over all natural numbers n, i and j with 1 ≤ i < j and 2j ≤ n; for integers, 2j ≤ n is the condition j ≤ n/2. It asks for a prime p with p ≥ i that divides the greatest common divisor of the binomial coefficients C(n, i) and C(n, j).
lean_target.text:
import Mathlib

def wishpool_target_prop : Prop :=
  ∀ n i j : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → i < j → 2 * j ≤ n →
    ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ i ≤ p ∧ p ∣ Nat.gcd (n.choose i) (n.choose j)

curated.name: The Erdős-Szekeres problem on a common prime factor at least i of two binomial coefficients (Erdős Problem 699)
curated.source_license: Licence of the source not determined on 2026-11-11; the statement is restated in the curator's own words.
curated.statement:
Question. Is it true that for all integers $1 \le i < j \le n/2$ there exists a prime $p \ge i$ dividing

$$\gcd\Bigl( \binom{n}{i}, \binom{n}{j} \Bigr)\,?$$

status_evidence.observed: Problem 699 has status state falsifiable, last update 2025-08-31. The latest commit touching the file is dated 2026-11-09. In this database the state falsifiable means open and resolvable by a finite counterexample.
The problem page (last edited 19 July 2026) describes partial results only and reports no resolution.
